reviews.comment: While ANTH210 isn't a very difficult course and it's very easy to get an A, my biggest struggle with Prof Lemus was that the structure of his lectures wasn't very organized, and he often went off on tangents during lecture time. Definitely read the textbook for this course and stay on top of the reading. You'll be teaching yourself a lot.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the chillest class ever. No exams all projects and they aren't very hard. Just make sure you do everything on the rubric and you should get an A. A few quizzes that weren't bad. Take this class for the core curriculum.

This will be the freest A of your life. There are 3 projects, all individual, super easy fieldwork stuff. MAYBE 1 weekly activity for homework. Quizzes are incredibly light. Attendance is non mandatory. Genuinely don't know why he doesn't have at least a 4 on here.

Do the work and you'll get an A. There are no exams but there are projects, they're done individually and not as a group so that helps. There are quizzes but they're easy and so is the homework. Project rubric is straight forward and easy to follow and he sticks to his syllabus pretty well.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lemus is a very chill and easygoing teacher, and whoever takes his ANTH 210 classes are essentially guaranteed an A as long as you do the bare minimum as to just do assignments and show up near the end of the semester for exit tickets. No exams or in class work, just 3 projects, quizzes, and Perusall activities which are outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very interesting guy and will probably talk about some fun/interesting stuff in class. He is very passionate and the class is extremely easy. Quizzes can be tricky but aren't super tough. Just look at the rubric for the projects and you are basically guaranteed to get 100s on them. No tests which was great. Completely free A.
He is a great prof who is always willing to help his students. He looks after everyone, is very clear about his submission deadlines and gives a ton of extra credit for simply attending class.

So easy. No exams, just quizzes and simple projects. Attendance isn't mandatory, but i go & work on stuff for other classes b/c he offers random extra credit. Not the best prof, but its b/c all of his work is easy, so lectures leave him free to ramble. His lectures arent designed to teach, but the class is so easy that ive never cared
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Online course, easy A. Perusall criteria is extremely lax, you can get over 80% just by clicking on every page or letting a video play to the end.

My biggest gripe is that while anthropology topics are probably important conversations to have, anthro papers can't make a point without everyone's brains leaking out of their ears in a 50 mile radius.

Professor Lemus is a really great guy! He is a bit hard to understand, but attendance is not required. The class is graded by 3 projects, 3 quizzes, and online activities so it is a pretty easy class. I do see him changing the attendance requirements, but he is a nice guy so it shouldn't be too bad.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guys great

Professor Lemus is a very nice person but not a good professor. He often rambled in class and did not provide much information over the topics. Attendance is not mandatory but he will make you feel bad if you don't go. The class was graded through activities on Perusall (very easy) and 3 big projects (also very easy). He is also hard to understand

Professor Lemus is very nice but not a great professor. he is very hard to understand and rambled a lot during class. Attendance is not mandatory but he will make you feel bad if you don't go. the class was solely graded on activity projects on Perusall (very easy... little work included) and 3 main projects(that are not hard at all).

I don't understand why this professor has a low rating. He's caring, approachable, and made the class easy and interesting. Attendance wasn't mandatory, although I think this will change, and projects were simple, involving observing people and writing about it. Quizzes were straightforward, and homework was easy, and no test! Highly recommend him!

Despite all of the other negative reviews, this class was the easiest A of my LIFE. No tests, 3 major projects that are a breeze, quizzes are online and open note. He does have a heavy accent which makes it hard to understand his lectures. HOWEVER, he is an easy grader. Weekly assignments that are not difficult at all to complete. Re-opens quizzes
I don't understand a word he says. He also doesn't really teach and just talks about the same stories and things every class. Study for the exams and you'll be fine but he's not the best lecturer.

4.0 engineering student here, I don't understand why universities employ people like this. This professor is a complete waste of money and time. Completely disorganized and rambling lecture on complete nonsense. Talking style of a child. He obviously has terrible reviews so why keep him? A&M should be embarrassed to employ professors like this.

This could have been an interesting class if the professor wasn't so bad. He doesn't talk about anything relevant to the exams during lecture. I don't think I learned a single thing all semester. The only way to get an A is to read the textbooks. He has a study guide for each exam but most of it wasn't on the tests. Take literally anyone else.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. I enrolled in this class thinking it would be interesting and an easy A. However, the disorganization of this professor made the class hard. His lectures consist of tangents that add no help to what we are trying to understand. The lectures are required due to in-class assignments every class. Reviews do not help either.

reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He never seemed to know what he was doing during the lectures; he would ramble on and on about random topics and ever actually teach anything meaningful. The tests were all based on the readings and slides. The tests were easy, but it was annoying as this was a class that I had actually looked forward to taking.

Tests as said before often had typos and misinformation, second attempts rarely if ever improved the grade. He is nearly impossible to reach through the email in the syllabus, and did not respond to me until a week later (despite follow ups) and only responded via Canvas, not email. Can't reach him or be sure of info... not a good combination.

The professor does allow two attempts for each exam, but there are many mistakes on each exam. On average, there was 4-6 questions that had typos or wrong information. As a result, the second attempt never helped. Many links inside the slides were broken even though he said he was going to fix them.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a good class to take over the summer! I took this class in a 5-week summer class and was easy! Make sure you keep up with lectures and with assignments, exams, and assignments were weighted heavily.

Professor Lemus is very unorganized. He would never post his lecture slides even though he said he would, and he rarely responded to emails in a timely manner. The exams were nothing like the study guides. I would spend hours reading the textbook and going over notes in preparation and still do poorly. Overall, please do not take him if able.

Most of the class is just participation, but the exams are very difficult. The powerpoints aren't always helpful since he doesn't go off the PowerPoint most of the time and don't know if you need to know that for the exams. Exams are most your actual grade and his study guides don't help much. Would take a different class for culture credit.

Professor Lemus grades on three things: attendance, in-class activities, and exams. He often goes off-topic, and his exams are not based on the review guides he gives. I don't recommend taking this class unless you are passionate about the topic. He does curve the overall grade at the end of the semester by like 1-2 points and gives extra credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although the class is a survey-level course on general anthropology, he focuses on a very niche book and niche topics instead. He gives extra credit, but they are singular percentages of points while nobody ever gets full points on his exams (even with his bonus questions). If you have the opportunity to take any other professor, I would.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of info from lectures and lots of readings. The class is weird; not impossible. Don't take if you despise some tangents (related to subject.) Go to his office hours if you need to or have questions, he's a good guy who will do what he can. Readings can be skimmed; don't neglect them. Tests are weird; hard to nail down preparing for them.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lemus is one of those liberal arts professors that REQUIRE you to come to class. He does nothing but speak off topic during lecture. Everything on the exam mostly comes from the textbook. If it weren't for attendance, I wouldn't even come to this laughable class. There is so much to memorize for the exams as well for a cultural credit course.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. He does not go over all of the material that shows up on the exams, and do not even think about bringing this up to him. Someone in my class did and he then asked if everyone else had the same opinion. To which the majority of the class replied "yes". He spent the rest of his lecturing making passive aggressive remarks.

Easy class if taken online. The material was sometimes interesting, and the tests seemed heavy on the lectures, but they also had a lot of information from elsewhere that I didn't recognize. A lot of the test was true/ false which made it difficult, especially since some of the questions were worded oddly. I didn't struggle to finish with an A.

Dr. Lemus was great! I had a couple struggles taking this course, but none that jeopardized my grade. There are very few grades, so tests are weighted heavily. Read the textbook and lecture material! You WILL make an A if you do. In addition, read the syllabus carefully. Some things in his syllabus were not correct and caused last minute changes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had a really hard time understanding the lectures because he went on a lot of illogical tangents. He released study guides for exams that had material we did not cover in class. Attendance worth 15% of your grade.
Hes a cool guy but has a strong accent which makes the lecture harder to follow. They are extremely boring too.

Overall, I think Lemus is a good professor even though his lectures can get a little bit rambly. However, he goes out of his way to make the class as easy as possible. As long as you go through his reviews and pay attention, you should be able to easily make an A. Just be sure to attend class for the points and keep up with the textbook readings.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a really easy class but extremely boring. I feel asleep almost every lecture and attendance is 15% of your final grade. 3 exams which aren't hard if you study and listen during lecture. His voice is very monotone and paying attention is difficult; I would recommend taking someone else. Only graded on exams and attendance.
